summary.opening: Queen's Gambit Declined: Harrwitz Attack, Fianchetto Defense

moments.name: 15…Re8
moments.headline: 15…Re8 is a mistake: Black's winning chances go from 51% to 34%.
points: White answers 16.exd5, which takes the pawn on d5.
Better was 15…Qd7 (−0.11): connects the rooks: development is complete and they can now support each other.
moments.better: 15…Qd7 connects the rooks. Engine line: 16.h3 Rad8 17.a3 f6 18.Bf4 a5 (−0.11).

moments.name: 16.Re3
moments.headline: 16.Re3 misses the chance 15…Re8 gave: 16.exd5 would have punished it. White's winning chances go from 66% to 48%.
points: Black answers 16…g6, which takes h5 away from the White queen on d1.
Better was 16.exd5 (+1.76), which takes the pawn on d5.
moments.better: 16.exd5 trades pawns and creates a passed pawn on d4. After 16…Qxd5 17.Be4 Qd7 18.Bxa8 Rxa8 19.d5 Qxd5 20.Qxd5 Bxd5 21.Bxg7 Be6, the queens come off and White comes out two pawns up (+1.76).

moments.name: 18.Rae1
moments.headline: 18.Rae1!! A real sacrifice: White gives up material and the engine still rates it best.
points: Leaves the rook on e3 where it can be taken.
Taking is too dangerous: Black's best reply is 18…Rc8 19.exd5 Bxd5 20.Be4 instead (the engine rates it −0.19).
18.Rae1 prepares exd5 and Be4.
The engine's plan continues with exd5 and Be4: this move is the first step.
Black answers 18…Rc8, leaving White with an isolated pawn on d4 and a king with pawns missing from its shelter.
After 18…Rc8 19.exd5 Bxd5 20.Be4 Bxe4 21.Rxe4 b4, the bishops are traded (−0.19).

why.title: The idea
why.text: 18.Rae1!! leaves the rook on e3 hanging. Taking it gives White the material back and more.

why.title: What White gives up
why.text: The rook on e3 is attacked by the bishop on g5, and 18.Rae1 doesn't save it. That's a whole rook on offer.

why.title: If Black takes the rook
why.text: 18…Bxe3 is met by 19.Rxe3, taking the bishop on e3. Then 20.Bxe4 takes the e4 pawn, and 21.Bb7 attacks the rook on c8. Material is level and White is a little better (+0.70).

why.title: Black's best try
why.text: Black's best is to leave the rook alone and play 18…Rc8. White answers 19.exd5, taking the d5 pawn and threatening dxe6, winning a bishop for a pawn. Then 20.Be4 threatens Bxd5, winning a bishop, and 21.Rxe4 takes the bishop on e4. White is a pawn down: White holds the balance (−0.19).

moments.name: 20.Qg3
moments.headline: 20.Qg3! The only good move here: every alternative is clearly worse.
points: Moves the attacked queen to safety.
Protects the h4 pawn, which was hanging.
The next best move, 20.hxg5, would drop White's winning chances from 50% to 12% (−5.32).
20.Qg3 gets the queen out of the way of …Bxf3.
Black was threatening …Bxf3, winning the queen for a bishop. The queen steps away.
Shores up the bishop on e5, which was under as much attack as it had defence (1 against 1).

moments.name: 25.Bxf5
moments.headline: 25.Bxf5 misses 25.Bxd8, which wins material. White's winning chances go from 56% to 17%.
points: Black answers 25…Rxe3, which takes the rook on e3.
After Rxe3, Black wins 2 points of material within 6 moves.
Better was 25.Bxd8 (+0.71), which takes the rook on d8.
moments.better: 25.Bxd8 wins the exchange and stops …h6. After 25…Rxe4 26.Rxe4 Bxe4 27.Bf6 h6 28.Qxb5 Bc6, the rooks are traded and White comes out a piece up (+0.71).

moments.name: 25…Rxe3
moments.headline: 25…Rxe3! The only good move here: every alternative is clearly worse.
points: Takes the rook on e3.
The next best move, 25…h6, would drop Black's winning chances from 83% to 44% (+0.69).
25…Rxe3 wins a bishop for a pawn and stops Bxd8.
Takes the rook on e3 and wins a bishop for a pawn once the captures settle.
White was threatening Bxd8, winning the exchange. Rxe3 takes care of it.
White answers 26.fxe3, taking back and taking d4 and f4 away from the queen, leaving Black with a king with pawns missing from its shelter.

moments.name: 26…h6
moments.headline: 26…h6! The only good move here: every alternative is clearly worse.
points: The pawn kicks the queen on g5, which has to move.
Makes an escape square for the king, so back-rank checks lose their sting.
The next best move, 26…Re8, would drop Black's winning chances from 82% to 21% (+3.56).
26…h6 wins a bishop for a pawn, picking it up with 27…Qxf6, and stops Bxd8.
Sets up a sequence and wins a bishop for a pawn once the captures settle, picking it up with 27…Qxf6.
White was threatening Bxd8, winning a rook. h6 takes care of it.

opening.name: Queen's Gambit Declined: Harrwitz Attack, Fianchetto Defense
points: Both sides followed opening theory up to 10…c4: 20 moves in all, 10 by White and 10 by Black.
Theory runs out after 10…c4: too few games between strong players reached this position to go further.
